title: darwin-memo: self-curating memory for LLM agents
description: Survival-selection memory for LLM agents. Lessons hold balances of a single conserved resource; a decide/settle/tick ledger credits and debits them from measured outcomes, charges upkeep, and buries entries that starve. No LLM judge is used in the mechanism, a design stance justified on cost and circularity grounds. This deposit archives version 0.5.1, which ships a technical report (paper/darwin-memo.md) on the cost and leanness of a judge-free conserved-resource buffer and a map of the noise regimes where it beats, ties, or loses to discrete strike counters, a successive-elimination bandit, and a local LLM judge, plus a frozen reproduction package (paper/reproduce.md, paper/reproduce.sh) with per-seed result JSON bound to a manifest. The report claims a cost argument, leanness, and an empirical noise-regime map, not a state-of-the-art result and not a demonstrated judge-free superiority.
